skill.name: iac-checkov
skill.description: Use Checkov to scan Infrastructure as Code for security misconfigurations, compliance gaps, secrets, and policy violations.
skill.summary: Guides Checkov scans, CI gates, compliance reporting, custom policies, and suppression review for IaC security.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The static findings are overwhelmingly documentation and template false positives: Markdown code fences, Checkov examples, skip paths, placeholders, and report parsing. I found no prompt injection, malware intent, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution path, but the CI templates should avoid mutable dependencies.

remediation.issue: Mutable CI dependencies in example workflows
remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to release tags or commit SHAs and pin container images to immutable tags or digests.

remediation.issue: Example templates may be copied directly into production
remediation.suggestion: Add comments that require users to review permissions, replace placeholders, and validate severity gates before adoption.

remediation.issue: Optional external module downloads can expand scan scope
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run module downloads only for trusted Terraform sources and to avoid scanning state files or secret-bearing directories.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Dependency References
semantic_findings.description: The CI templates use mutable references such as bridgecrewio/checkov-action@master and bridgecrew/checkov:latest. Users who copy these templates could receive unreviewed upstream changes in security-sensitive pipelines.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mutable action branch and latest container tag are directly present in CI examples. This is a common supply-chain hardening issue, though it is not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Infrastructure teams need fast feedback on risky cloud configuration before deployment. This skill guides Checkov scans, policy tuning, and compliance reporting for IaC workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Checkov scan commands for Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfile, Helm, and secrets frameworks.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and pre-commit workflows.
Shows how to configure baselines, severity gates, skipped checks, and output formats.
Guides custom Checkov policy creation with Python and YAML examples.
Maps findings to CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, NIST, and GDPR reporting needs.
Documents suppression governance with review, expiration, and compensating control guidance.
limitations: It depends on Checkov and related command-line tools being installed by the user or CI environment.
It does not replace manual security review for accepted risk or complex architecture decisions.
Compliance mappings need validation against current organizational control requirements.
Some examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production use.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge IaC security review
use_cases.description: Run Checkov on pull requests and block critical Terraform, Kubernetes, or Dockerfile misconfigurations before merge.

use_cases.title: Compliance evidence preparation
use_cases.description: Generate Checkov reports aligned to CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, NIST, or GDPR review workflows.

use_cases.title: Custom policy rollout
use_cases.description: Create organization-specific Checkov policies and test them against sample infrastructure before CI enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Run a first scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run a basic Checkov scan on my Terraform directory. Explain the command, expected output, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI security gating
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Checkov CI gate for Terraform and Kubernetes. It should fail on critical and high findings and keep reports as artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Review suppressions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Checkov suppressions for risk. Identify weak justifications, missing approvals, and better compensating controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a custom policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design and test a custom Checkov policy for required cloud resource tags and compliance reporting.

output_examples.input: User asks for a Terraform scan plan for a new repository.
output_examples.output: A concise scan workflow with framework selection, output formats, baseline advice, and severity gate recommendations.

output_examples.input: User asks whether a Checkov suppression is acceptable.
output_examples.output: A risk review covering business justification, compensating controls, expiration, approval requirements, and follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: User asks for compliance reporting guidance.
output_examples.output: A checklist that links Checkov outputs to audit evidence, report retention, and control owner review.

best_practices: Start with a baseline, then fail builds only on new critical and high findings.
Require clear business justification and review for every high-risk suppression.
Pin CI actions and container images to stable versions or digests before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not suppress Checkov findings without an owner, expiration date, and risk rationale.
Do not scan Terraform state files or directories that may contain secrets.
Do not copy example CI templates into production without pinning dependencies and reviewing permissions.

faq.question: What IaC frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Dockerfile, Helm, ARM, secrets scanning, and related CI workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run Checkov automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. The user or CI environment runs Checkov commands.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Checkov output formats and mappings for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, NIST, and GDPR workflows.

faq.question: Can it create custom Checkov policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Python and YAML custom policies, plus testing and loading examples.

faq.question: How should teams handle false positives?
faq.answer: Use documented suppressions with approval, compensating controls, expiration dates, and periodic review.

faq.question: What should be changed before production use?
faq.answer: Pin mutable CI dependencies, review permissions, replace placeholders, and align severity gates with team policy.
